original_question: For the moduli space M_{2n}^{K3} of polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2n, do the Noether-Lefschetz divisor classes generate the rational Picard group, i.e., do they span Pic(M_{2n}^{K3}) tensor Q?
target_in_paper: Question 7 in section (iv), "On the moduli of K3 surfaces".
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical target of the paper very closely: it identifies the same moduli space M^{K3}_{2n}, asks about Noether-Lefschetz divisors in codimension 1, and formulates the issue as whether they span the rational Picard group. This is essentially Pandharipande's Q7.
missing_details: The paper explicitly defines M^{K3}_{2n} as the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) with degree L^2 = 2n.
The nearby context says the Noether-Lefschetz loci parametrize polarized K3 surfaces with higher-rank Picard lattices; this should be stated so that "Noether-Lefschetz divisors" is stand-alone.
The question is asked for a fixed degree 2n (that is, for a given n), not as one single universal statement over all n at once.
The coefficient extension is exactly Pic(M^{K3}_{2n}) ⊗_Z Q, so the issue is rational linear span of divisor classes.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should remain only about divisor classes in the Picard group, not about the full tautological ring or higher-codimension Noether-Lefschetz loci; that broader neighboring problem is Q6, not Q7.
refined_question: For a fixed degree 2n, let M^{K3}_{2n} denote the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) with L^2 = 2n. The Noether-Lefschetz loci in M^{K3}_{2n} parametrize polarized K3 surfaces whose Picard lattices have higher rank. Do the classes of the Noether-Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group Pic(M^{K3}_{2n}) ⊗_Z Q?
justification: The exact statement your draft is aiming at is Pandharipande's Q7. The immediately preceding sentences in the same K3 section supply the only definitions needed to make Q7 self-contained: what M^{K3}_{2n} denotes, what degree 2n means, and what the Noether-Lefschetz loci are. Your draft is already very close; the refinement only restores those explicit definitions and keeps the scope at the Picard-group level, exactly as in the paper.
